copy.title: The Bloomberg Money File
copy.desc: An interactive, fully sourced map of Michael Bloomberg’s family: the company he owns 88% of, the campaigns he paid for, the billions he gives away, and the money on the public record.
copy.eyebrow: File #030 · The Bloomberg family · Data as of
copy.h1: The mayor who sold data terminals is giving billions away. We followed the money.
copy.lede: Who’s who, what he owns, what he spent on politics, what he gives away, and the money on the public record. Every number links to its source.
copy.familyLede: Tap anyone to open their file. Michael’s two daughters are adults; both work on the family’s giving.
copy.investLede: You can’t buy shares in Bloomberg LP: it is private, and Michael owns about 88% of it. Everything else here is a charity or a nonprofit.
copy.moneyLede: Almost all of it is his stake in Bloomberg LP, which Forbes says brings in about $15 billion a year in revenue. Only Michael has a published net worth.
copy.recordLede: What federal election filings, deal announcements and giving records show. Filings and reporting, not guesses.
copy.trailLede: From a $9,000-a-year Wall Street job to one of the biggest donors in America.

summary.t: A bookkeeper for a dairy company. He died suddenly while Michael was in college; a Harvard professorship Michael later endowed is named for him.
Born Charlotte Rubens. She raised Michael and his sister, Marjorie.
Since February 2002 she has been New York City’s commissioner for the United Nations, consular corps and protocol, starting with her brother’s first term as mayor.
Founded the financial data and news company Bloomberg LP in 1981 after being fired from Salomon Brothers. He was mayor of New York City from 2002 to 2013 and ran for president in 2020.

owns.t: Founder; owns about 88%. He has pledged the stake to Bloomberg Philanthropies on his death, or sooner.

record.t: Salomon Brothers hired him in 1966 for $9,000 a year. When new owners fired him in 1981, they paid him $10 million for his equity. He started his own company that year.
In July 2008 his company agreed to buy back the 20% of Bloomberg LP owned by Merrill Lynch for $4.425 billion.
He spent about $73 million of his own money to win the 2001 mayoral race. His 2020 presidential run cost him $935 million through February 2020, his campaign’s federal filing showed.
He gave $4.3 billion in 2025, more than any other American donor for the third year running, and more than $25.4 billion over his lifetime.

facts.t: His first gift to Johns Hopkins, his alma mater, was $5 in 1965. He has since given it more than $4.55 billion, including $1.8 billion in 2018 for need-blind admission and $1 billion in 2024 to make medical school free for students from families earning under $300,000.
He signed the Giving Pledge in 2010.

summary.t: A former New York State superintendent of banks. She and Michael have been partners since 2000.

worth.none: No published estimate of her own.

summary.t: Founder and CEO of Murmuration, a nonprofit that supports civic engagement. She sits on the board of Bloomberg Philanthropies and worked in her father’s mayoral office.

facts.t: She and Georgina run the Emma and Georgina Bloomberg Foundation, which funds education and animal rights groups.

summary.t: A show jumper who has won several competitions. She co-runs a family foundation with her sister.

companies.name: Bloomberg LP
companies.t: Sells the Bloomberg Terminal and runs Bloomberg News, with about $15 billion in yearly revenue, per Forbes. Vlad Kliatchko is CEO; Michael has pledged his stake to Bloomberg Philanthropies.

companies.name: Bloomberg Philanthropies
companies.t: His charitable organization, not a business. It funds public health, the arts, government innovation, the environment and education.

companies.name: Murmuration
companies.t: A nonprofit that supports community-driven civic engagement.
